paragraphs.text: Mitochondrial myopathy with lactic acidosis (MMLA) is an autosomal recessive mitochondrial disorder caused by biallelic variants in PNPLA8, which encodes calcium-independent phospholipase A2-gamma (iPLA2-gamma). Patients can have progressive muscle weakness, lactic acidosis, and structurally abnormal mitochondria in muscle (Saunders et al., 2015; Shukla et al., 2018). The phenotype forms a continuum. At the severe end is a congenital-onset form with congenital microcephaly, early-onset epileptic encephalopathy, and early death. Intermediate forms include infantile- and childhood-onset neurodegeneration with progressive microcephaly. At the mild end is an adolescent- or adult-onset form with cerebellar ataxia and peripheral neuropathy (Abdel-Hamid et al., 2024; Nakamura et al., 2024).

paragraphs.text: Saunders et al. (2015) reported a 7-year-old girl (CMH193) who was evaluated for suspected mitochondrial myopathy. In her first year she was asymptomatic and met developmental milestones, apart from toe-walking. She had a positive Gowers sign at age 2 years and could no longer walk by age 3 years. Her course was progressive, with proximal muscle weakness, declining fine motor skills, dysarthria, dysmetria, and dystonia. Her hypotonia progressed to spasticity. She had complex partial seizures with left temporal lobe spikes on EEG. Her body habitus was very lean and she did not gain weight. She had significant lactic acidosis that required bicarbonate supplementation. A muscle biopsy at age 4 showed variable fiber size with isolated small atrophic fibers and no ragged red fibers. On electron microscopy, mitochondria showed marked disarray of cristae and globular dense osmiophilic inclusions. There were subsarcolemmal aggregates of abnormal mitochondria with concentric lamellar membranes, suggesting degenerating mitochondria, and secondary lysosomes were increased. Brain MRI at 33 months showed subtle increased signal in the medial globus pallidus bilaterally, which was no longer seen 2 years later.

At birth she had congenital microcephaly, with a head circumference of 29 cm (-4 SD). Multifocal clonic seizures began on day 2 of life, and she had spasticity of all 4 limbs. Brain MRI showed microcephaly with a simplified gyral pattern, hypoplasia of the corpus callosum, a prominent cisterna magna with a hypoplastic cerebellum, and brainstem atrophy. MRS showed an elevated lipid-lactate peak. TORCH testing was negative.

paragraphs.text: Shukla et al. (2018) also described a girl of India/Fiji origin born to nonconsanguineous parents (patient 2). She developed normally until about 13 months of age and then regressed, with episodes of epilepsia partialis continua and focal seizures. She remained at an 8-month developmental level, did not speak, and needed a gastrostomy tube. She developed acquired microcephaly, with a head circumference of -4.7 SD at 15 years. Other features were hypotonia, proximal muscle weakness, absent reflexes, choreiform movements, dystonia, and contractures. She also had hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with subaortic stenosis and obstructive sleep apnea. Visual evoked potentials had severely reduced amplitudes. Serial MRI showed progressive atrophy of the cerebellum, brainstem, and cerebrum, with thinning of the corpus callosum. MRS showed a persistent lipid-lactate peak. Blood lactate was elevated, and GDF15 was elevated at 1293 pg/ml.

paragraphs.text: Burnyte et al. (2023) described 2 adult Lithuanian sibs, a brother and a sister. Both had slowly progressive ataxia beginning between ages 10 and 14 years, accompanied by progressive sensorimotor axonal polyneuropathy, and cognition was preserved in both. The brother's symptoms began at age 14 years with lower limb weakness, distal muscle atrophy, ataxia, and gait disturbance. From age 17 years he could not walk without assistance. He later developed tetraparesis, absent lower limb reflexes, bilateral Babinski signs, foot deformities, dysmetria, and distal hypoesthesia. At age 45 years he had mild dysarthria and horizontal nystagmus, his MMSE score was normal, and brain MRI showed mild cerebellar atrophy. The sister developed walking difficulty and weakness in both lower limbs at age 14 years. When examined at age 21 she had distal limb muscle atrophy, absent lower limb reflexes, bilateral Babinski signs, severe axial ataxia, and appendicular dysmetria, and she could not keep an upright posture. Her cranial nerves and cognition were normal. Nerve conduction studies showed an axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy, and EMG showed no myopathic changes.

paragraphs.text: Nakamura et al. (2024) reported 14 patients from 12 unrelated families. Common features were central hypotonia (13 of 13), dystonia (8 of 12), seizures (10 of 14), and cerebellar atrophy (12 of 12). The 8 patients in Families 1 through 8 were severely affected. In this group, 5 of 7 had congenital microcephaly, 7 of 7 had global developmental delay with no milestones attained, 7 of 8 had peripheral spasticity, and 8 of 8 had seizure onset within 7 months of age. Neuroimaging in the severe group showed a simplified gyral pattern (6 of 6), pontocerebellar hypoplasia (7 of 7), and severe progressive cerebral atrophy (5 of 5). The 2 patients in Families 9 and 10 were of intermediate severity. The 4 patients in Families 11 and 12, from Iran and Egypt, had a relatively mild phenotype. All 4 attained walking and all 4 had regression of milestones. Ataxia was present in 3 of 4, and intellectual disability was mild or absent in 3 of 4. Seizures were unique or absent in all 4. Brain MRI in the mild group showed little or no cerebral volume loss but progressive cerebellar atrophy.

paragraphs.text: Nakamura et al. (2024) used exome or genome sequencing to identify biallelic ultra-rare PNPLA8 variants in 14 individuals with neurological manifestations from 12 unrelated families. There were 6 males and 8 females, aged 3 days to 33 years. The 14 variants, 12 of them novel, comprised 4 nonsense, 5 frameshift, 3 intronic variants near exon-intron boundaries, and 2 missense variants. Each had a population frequency below 0.001%. Patient 1, a Japanese boy, carried c.1625+3_1625+6del. In his lymphoblastoid cells this variant caused skipping of exons 6 to 8, and his skin fibroblasts showed a significant reduction of the 77-kDa PNPLA8 protein, which the authors interpreted as a null effect. Patient 2 carried the splice variant c.2075-2A-G and Patient 5 carried c.1684-2A-G. No patient cells were available for these 2 patients, but SpliceAI predicted loss of the splice acceptor site for each variant (delta scores 0.97 and 0.93, respectively). The authors also studied PNPLA8 protein in patient fibroblasts. The p.Glu296LysfsTer6 variant from severely affected Patient 6 had a null effect. Fibroblasts from mildly affected Patient 12 (p.Leu759AlafsTer4) and from non-neuronal Patient 14 (p.Val7Ter) showed weak expression of the 77-kDa protein, suggesting residual function. Fibroblasts from a previously reported, severely affected patient homozygous for the missense variant p.Val520Asp expressed PNPLA8 at levels similar to controls.

paragraphs.text: Mancuso et al. (2007) generated mice null for iPLA2-gamma (Pnpla8) by eliminating the enzyme's active site through homologous recombination. The null mice had multiple bioenergetic dysfunctional phenotypes, including growth retardation, cold intolerance, and reduced exercise endurance. After transverse aortic constriction, mortality from cardiac stress was greatly increased. Mitochondrial function was abnormal, with a 65% decrease in ascorbate-induced complex IV-mediated oxygen consumption. Myocardial cardiolipin content was reduced and the mix of cardiolipin molecular species was altered. The authors concluded that iPLA2-gamma is essential for efficient mitochondrial bioenergetic function because it shapes mitochondrial membrane lipid metabolism and composition.

paragraphs.text: Song et al. (2010) fed a high-fat Western diet to iPLA2-gamma-knockout and wildtype mice. Compared with wildtype mice, the knockout mice were resistant to diet-induced increases in body weight, adiposity, and blood cholesterol, glucose, and insulin. This was despite similar food intake and similar digestion and absorption of dietary fat. The knockout mice were also relatively resistant to diet-induced insulin resistance, glucose intolerance, and changes in the balance of fat versus carbohydrate fuel use. Knockout skeletal muscle had impaired mitochondrial beta-oxidation of fatty acids. On the Western diet, knockout muscle and liver accumulated more long-chain acylcarnitine species than wildtype tissue. The knockout mice also excreted more long-chain acylcarnitine in urine and deposited much less triacylglycerol in the liver.

paragraphs.text: Yoda et al. (2010) found that iPLA2-gamma (Pnpla8)-knockout mice were born at the expected mendelian ratio and appeared normal and healthy at 1 month of age. Growth retardation began at 2 months, and kyphosis and significant muscle weakness were present by 4 months. On electron microscopy, knockout skeletal muscle showed swollen mitochondria, fewer mitochondria, and atrophy of myofilaments. Knockout muscle also showed increased lipid peroxidation and induction of several oxidative stress-related genes. The composition of cardiolipin and of other phospholipid subclasses was altered, and levels of myoprotective prostanoids were reduced. The authors concluded that loss of iPLA2-gamma causes mitochondrial dysfunction and increased oxidative stress, leading to loss of skeletal muscle structure and function. They also suggested that iPLA2-gamma may help modulate the production of lipid mediators in vivo.

paragraphs.text: Hirabayashi et al. (2023) reported that in the liver, PNPLA8 and PNPLA7 form a phospholipase/lysophospholipase pathway that breaks down membrane phosphatidylcholine into water-soluble glycerophosphocholine (GPC). This process makes choline stored in hepatic phosphatidylcholine available for methyl metabolism and for replenishing the methionine cycle. PNPLA8-deficient mice reproduced most of the phenotypes of PNPLA7-deficient mice. These included growth retardation, hypoglycemia, hypolipidemia, increased energy consumption, reduced adiposity, and increased FGF21. They also included an altered histone/DNA methylation landscape, which the authors attributed to methionine insufficiency. Unlike wildtype mice fed a methionine/choline-deficient diet, the knockout mice had decreased hepatic triglyceride. The authors suggested this was likely due to reduced lipogenesis and reduced GPC-derived glycerol flux.

paragraphs.text: Moon et al. (2023) generated a skeletal muscle-specific iPLA2-gamma knockout mouse (SKMiPLA2gammaKO). They crossed mice carrying loxP sites flanking exon 5, which encodes the enzyme active site, with transgenic mice expressing Cre recombinase from the human alpha-actin promoter. Western blot analysis of mitochondria from white adipose tissue, liver, and skeletal muscle confirmed that ablation was restricted to skeletal muscle. The knockout mice had pronounced muscle weakness, muscle atrophy, and increased blood lactate. These resulted from defects in mitochondrial function that impaired pyruvate processing and caused bioenergetic inefficiency. Tibialis anterior and quadriceps muscle mass was decreased by 30% in males, and females had a greater loss of tibialis anterior mass. Transmission electron microscopy of tibialis anterior muscle from 7-month-old knockout mice showed a prevalence of mitochondria with severe ultrastructural damage, including irregular cristae and electron-dense inclusions, along with disruption of normal striated muscle structure. Histology showed internalized nuclei and smaller myocyte diameter in tibialis anterior. Quadriceps showed irregularly sized myocytes and more markedly small myofibers. Myogenin expression was markedly increased while MyoD was unchanged, indicating more active regenerative myogenesis. The fast-twitch tibialis anterior was further shifted toward a fast-twitch type II fiber phenotype.

paragraphs.text: In skeletal muscle of SKMiPLA2gammaKO mice, Moon et al. (2023) found that mitochondrial DNA copy number was significantly decreased. Protein levels of the mitochondrial fusion/fission proteins DRP1, OPA1, and MFN1 were dramatically diminished, despite only modest decreases in their mRNA levels. Mitochondrial markers (VDAC, ANT, and citrate synthase) were unchanged. Protein synthesis through the Akt/mTOR/S6 pathway was significantly impaired, whereas autophagic flux was unchanged. The authors concluded that reduced net protein synthesis in the setting of bioenergetic inefficiency likely underlay the muscle atrophy.

paragraphs.text: In functional tests, Moon et al. (2023) found that 7- to 8-month-old SKMiPLA2gammaKO mice had weaker grip force and fatigued more rapidly during treadmill exercise, regardless of diet or sex. After treadmill exercise, serum lactate rose more in knockout than wildtype mice, even though average exercise duration was shorter. In high-intensity treadmill exercise at 18 m/min for 4 minutes, 3 of 6 knockout females were completely exhausted within 1 to 2.5 minutes. Blood lactate accumulation was markedly increased in knockout mice, with a corresponding decline in blood glucose. Ex vivo, extensor digitorum longus muscle weight and body weight were lower in knockout mice, but specific tetanic peak tension normalized to cross-sectional area did not differ between genotypes. The authors noted that this limited their ability to exclude neurologic or behavioral contributions to the weakness.

paragraphs.text: Moon et al. (2023) used high-resolution respirometry and found that tibialis anterior mitochondria from male SKMiPLA2gammaKO mice on normal chow consumed 50% less oxygen than wildtype controls with glutamate/pyruvate/malate as substrate. The difference was even larger in females. Protein levels of complex IV and cytochrome c were dramatically reduced. Complex I and II protein levels were unchanged, but their catalytic activities were decreased by about 50% and 25%, respectively. Mitochondrial membrane potential was significantly lower with either complex I or complex II substrates, and hydrogen peroxide production from forward and reverse electron transfer was greatly attenuated. Shotgun lipidomics showed significantly lower levels of tetra-18:2 cardiolipin, the most abundant mature cardiolipin species in skeletal muscle, and decreased 22:6-containing cardiolipin species. The authors suggested that loss of tetra-18:2 cardiolipin contributes to inefficient respiration by disrupting the stability and association of electron transport chain proteins.

paragraphs.text: On a high-fat diet, SKMiPLA2gammaKO mice were resistant to weight gain, gaining about 8 g on average after 3 months compared with about 16 g in wildtype mice (Moon et al., 2023). They showed improved glucose clearance, with a lower peak glucose (about 240 vs about 320 mg/dL) and a decreased area under the curve, but insulin tolerance and serum insulin levels did not differ significantly. Compared with wildtype mice, the knockout mice had dramatically less hepatic lipid droplet content, significantly lower hepatic triacylglycerol and diacylglycerol species, no increase in liver-to-body weight ratio, diminished diet-induced fibrosis, and higher hepatic glycogen. In contrast, diet-induced increases in white adipose tissue mass were significantly more prominent in the knockout mice. Moon et al. (2023) concluded that iPLA2-gamma supports skeletal muscle bioenergetic function by preserving mitochondrial structural and functional integrity, maintaining an appropriate membrane environment for assembly of protein complexes, and coordinating signaling between skeletal muscle and liver. They concluded that the knockout phenotype reflected multifactorial mitochondrial dysfunction with no single identifiable precipitating cause.

paragraphs.text: In a 27-year-old Chinese woman with cerebellar ataxia, tremors, and primary ovarian insufficiency, Chen et al. (2024) used whole-exome sequencing to identify compound heterozygous mutations in the PNPLA8 gene. One was a c.1777T-G transversion resulting in a tyr593-to-asp (Y593D) substitution. The other was a frameshift mutation, c.1515_1516delTT (p.Tyr506SerfsTer27). The variants were inherited from her parents.
